messages:
maria: heads up — ran into a canary flip yesterday where traffic didn't fail over cleanly to the stable pool. app user saw 502s for ~90s. filing this here to coordinate a small oncall follow-up and a longer-term refactor.
alex: ugh, thanks for flagging. any quick root cause? routing, health checks, or model variant mismatch?
sam: looks like router retried but some backends returned 500s and the retry window overlapped with a new canary config push. state machine got inconsistent.
maria: exactly. sequence was: canary start -> probe failures -> our soft-fallback policy attempted partial switchover -> concurrent deploy touched routing config -> race -> both routes had partial clients. recovery was manual quorum flip.
oncall-bot: incident-#2113334444 created — priority P2, alerted oncall.
chris: quick suggestion for oncall playbook: ensure the failure detector has a cooldown + a single authoritative coordinator for switch decisions. Avoid distributed decision without a leader.
alex: agree. short-term we should widen probe window to avoid oscillation (eg increase probe cool-down from 5s -> 20s) and make rollbacks atomic per-route.
sam: that helps but still brittle. long-term idea: split decisioning out of the router into a separate "switchboard" service that owns rollout state and exposes a simple decisional API.
maria: can you sketch the API? I want to make sure we don't introduce new latency in hot paths.
sam: simple RPC:

```
POST /decide
body: {route_id, current_metrics, goal: "canary"}
response: {action: "stay", "promote", "rollback", reason: "xmetric > threshold"}
```

router then fetches decision (cached for 1s) and executes. decision service pulls metrics with its own aggregator.
chris: nice. this centralizes complexity and lets us add safe sequencing (mutex per route), canary timeouts, and human overrides.
alex: tradeoffs: more network calls + new failure mode (decision service outage). mitigate by local fallback policy in router that can operate if decision service unreachable.
maria: for reliability we should design the router to operate in three modes: authoritative (decision service), degraded-local (cached policy), and fail-open (route to stable only).
sam: also add a signed epoch token from switchboard so routers can detect stale decisions during config churn.
alex: operationally, we need metrics: time-to-detect, time-to-recover, false-positive rate for probes, and decision latency percentiles. add them to the canary dashboard.
maria: action items:
- sam: prototype switchboard API + epoch token (ETA 2w)
- alex: update oncall playbook to increase probe cooldown + atomic route flip step (ETA tomorrow)
- chris: design doc for modes (authoritative/degraded/fail-open) + rollback circuit (ETA 1w)
- oncall-bot: schedule a follow-up war room if we see >1 similar incident in 7d

sam: one more note — we should define a canary contract for models: compatible KV cache schema, tokenizer version, and max sequence length. fallback should only promote variants that satisfy the contract.
maria: agreed. if we add that, we reduce bad-fallbacks where model mismatch causes 5xxs. put that requirement into model onboarding checklist.
alex: 👍 I'll add checklist item and a small validation step in the switchboard that rejects incompatible promotions.
chris: think about gradual promotion windows too: promote x% -> measure -> promote y% -> full. the switchboard can own that and expose per-step timers.
maria: great thread. i'll capture this in a short RFC follow-up and ping infra + runtime for review. thanks all :heart:
